$comment: The committed tenant-isolation case table for COV-06. EVERY NEGATIVE CASE IS PRECEDED BY A POSITIVE CONTROL ON THE SAME TABLE WITH THE SAME VERB, because a denial and an empty table are indistinguishable from the negative alone — before the API-role grants landed, every table answered 42501 to every role, so 'org A sees none of org B's rows' was true only because org A saw no rows at all. A suite whose positive control fails is a RED suite, not a green one. The two negative outcomes are deliberately different expectations: 'no-rows' is the row-level-security outcome (the request succeeded and returned nothing), while 'denied' is the missing-grant outcome (the request failed with PostgREST code 42501). Collapsing them would stop a red run from saying whether RLS or a grant produced it. No uuid, email or token appears in this file: the script resolves every id from frontend/supabase/fixtures.json at runtime, which scripts/check-seed-fixture.mjs keeps in agreement with seed.sql.
